---
title: "Far away and Up close"
date: 2026-08-04
---

I’m on a downhill journey, though an interesting one, to say the least. Somehow, I am standing exactly where I thought I’d never be.

I wished J a happy birthday, but I couldn't reply to her that same day because of a few personal commitments. I saw her message, set it aside, and meant to get back to it later. I didn't look back for a couple of days, only to find that her response, a simple "I'm fine, thanks. How are you?" had been deleted. I assume she thought it was personal and overthought it? Either way, not my beeswax. But it weirded me out, and I couldn't bring myself to reply to any of her messages after that. Maybe she felt like she forced a connection, and when it didn't work, felt it backfire? Great. Now I'm overthinking.

Is it my responsibility to check if the people around me are doing okay? It’s not like they’re alone., in fact, it’s the exact opposite. Nobody was there when I needed someone. Still, I wouldn't wish that isolation on anyone. I want to be there for others, I just don't know how. I’m so wrapped up in the traps of my own making that I can't see more than a few feet ahead of me. I can't fix people... can I?

I’m not sure if I’m causing a scene with those around me, but I genuinely can't act any other way. It’s painstakingly hard given the amount of pain I’m in. All day, every day, I picture myself suffocating in brutal ways and I can't stop it. The air in the room gets lower and lower, and I can feel myself slowly choking. Can I talk to anyone about this? No. Why? Fear of judgment.

"I hope either all of us or none of us are judged based on our worst mistakes."
-- Ted Lasso

I have to redeem myself. That takes time, along with the power to believe that everything will be okay, eventually. Why wouldn't it be?

Then again, maybe being free is a burden in itself.
